description: CREWCARE is a team interested in technology, space exploration, and using data to solve real-world problems.For NASA Space Apps 2026, we're building a health monitoring software concept for astronauts. We bring together Machine Learning, Software Development, UI/UX, and Research to explore new ideas and build useful solutions.
summary: CREWCARE is a web-based crew health companion for astronauts on missions from low Earth orbit to the Moon and Mars. The crew logs vital signs and spacecraft readings (heart rate, SpO2, temperature, sleep, radiation, cabin CO2, Earth communication delay). A machine-learning model classifies the crew’s state as Normal, Warning, or Critical and returns step-by-step actions the astronaut can take on board. This matters because, on deep-space missions, communication delays of up to 22 minutes mean the crew cannot wait for Earth to respond. CREWCARE supports NASA’s Human Research Program hazards by helping astronauts detect problems early, act autonomously, and send a clear summary to flight surgeons.
details:
What it does:

CREWCARE is a unified, nine-page onboard health dashboard designed for non-physician astronauts:

- Overview: Live risk banner, vital cards, and seven-day trends.

- Daily Health Check: A three-step wizard (vitals and cabin telemetry, sleep and mood, review) with live risk evaluation.

- Health Analytics: Heart rate, blood pressure, temperature, glucose, and sleep history tracked against a personal baseline.

- Human Body Map: Interactive education on five body systems affected by spaceflight.

- Alerts & Actions: Automatically created alerts, review status, and a structured downlink summary for Earth.

- Sleep & Mental Wellness: Sleep, mood, and stress logs, plus a guided two-minute breathing exercise.

- Space Health Guide: Searchable reference library linked to NASA sources.

- Mission Routine: Daily task and countermeasure tracking.

- Settings: Units, accessibility, and crew profile.

How it works:

Six readings (heart rate, SpO2, sleep duration, radiation, cabin CO2, and Earth communication delay) are sent to a local Python API (Starlette) running a scikit-learn pipeline (StandardScaler + Random Forest, 200 trees). It classifies risk into Normal, Warning, or Critical and returns three immediate recommended actions. If the AI microservice is offline, the PHP backend and JavaScript frontend fall back immediately to a deterministic rule-based engine with identical thresholds so the crew always receives an assessment. Radiation thresholds adapt across four mission profiles: Spacecraft (LEO), ISS, Lunar Base (Artemis), and Mars Transit. Mars Transit activates an Autonomous Medical Mode for communication delays of 4 to 22 minutes, building store-and-forward medical summary packets for flight surgeons. Warning and Critical results automatically create alerts in the database, with strict per-user record isolation.

Benefits, Creativity & Intended Impact:

CREWCARE bridges the medical autonomy gap in deep space by shifting from raw telemetry display to actionable, context-aware clinical guidance tailored for non-physicians. Its dual-engine fail-safe architecture guarantees 100% offline reliability, while personal baselines catch subtle physiological shifts early. On Earth, this offline-first triage model can support remote clinics, maritime crews, and disaster-response teams lacking immediate physician access.

Tools, Languages & Software Used:

PHP 8.2, MySQL (PDO), JavaScript, HTML5/CSS3, Chart.js, Font Awesome, Python 3, scikit-learn, pandas, NumPy, joblib, and Starlette/Uvicorn. No special hardware is required; readings are entered manually in this educational prototype, and the modular architecture supports future wearable sensor integration.
